items.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
items.snippet: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.

This process, known as high-harmonic generation, provides a powerful way to investigate the rapid motion of electrons in solids. items.title: New model reveals how water moves through tile-drained farm fields
items.snippet: Tile drainage fundamentally alters how water moves through agricultural fields, affecting surface ponding, water-table dynamics, crop growth, nutrient transport and water quality. Yet fields with similar drainage systems can respond differently depending on soil, topography and tile design—differences that most models struggle to resolve at the field scale.

items.title: An atlas of vanished places: How climate change is rewriting the books on our shelves
items.snippet: On Aug. 26, 2026, a huge mass of rock and ice broke away at an altitude of around 5,200 meters (17,100 feet) in the Himalayas. Within minutes, it became an avalanche of debris and water that hurtled down toward the Nepal-Tibet border, with such force that the seismic signals were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

items.title: New research finds AI adoption is associated with more managers—and different managerial skills
items.snippet: A Strategic Management Journal study challenges the assumption that AI adoption automatically reduces demand for managers. Liudmila Alekseeva, José Azar, Mireia Giné and Sampsa Samila analyze U.S. job postings from 2010 to 2022, linking firm-level AI adoption with managerial vacancies and skill requirements.

items.title: Gender differences in values are not widening in Europe after all
items.snippet: In recent years, public discussion has focused on the increasingly conservative values of young men. A recently published study indicates that this is primarily a phenomenon prominent in social and conventional media, not an overall trend.

items.title: How restaurants can make sustainable dining choices easier while still making a profit
items.snippet: Canadians are eating out less. A 2025 survey found 57% of them are cooking at home more often to save money, while 69% of restaurant operators say customers are dining out less because of affordability. According to Restaurants Canada, 41% of operators are either losing money or breaking even.
